questions.q: According to this lesson, what's wrong with giving a new hire "the same access as" an existing employee doing a similar job?
options: It propagates whatever access accumulated on that account, including leftover or over-granted permissions, instead of examining what the job actually requires
It always grants too little access to the new hire
It is the recommended best-practice approach to RBAC design
It is technically impossible in most identity systems
questions.explain: Cloning an account copies its history along with its legitimate access, including permissions the original person no longer needs.

options: A built-in Azure RBAC command for listing role assignments
Analyzing real permission usage and job responsibilities to identify the natural role groupings an organization already has
Randomly assigning users to existing roles to simplify administration
Deleting roles that haven't been used in 90 days
questions.explain: Role mining looks at evidence of how people actually work to propose roles, rather than inventing them from an org chart.

options: A security vulnerability where roles automatically grant admin access
The failure mode where near-duplicate roles are created for every small access variation instead of reusing a shared base role
The process of merging many roles into one broad role
A term for when a single role is assigned to too many users
questions.explain: Role explosion produces hundreds of barely-distinct roles that nobody can meaningfully audit, defeating RBAC's purpose.

questions.q: Why does role explosion undermine the point of RBAC?
options: It makes role assignments execute more slowly
It is only a cosmetic issue with no real security impact
It automatically grants excess permissions to every user
It turns a system meant to be reviewable through a small number of well-understood roles into one with too many near-duplicate roles to audit
questions.explain: RBAC's value depends on a manageable number of roles; a role per minor variation makes genuine review impractical.

questions.q: What is the safe sequencing for designing a new role, according to this lesson?
options: Start with the minimum access the job function provably needs, and add specific access only when a documented need arises
Grant every possible permission so no one ever has to request more
Copy the broadest existing role in the organization and reuse it everywhere
Start broad with full access, then plan to narrow it down later
questions.explain: Starting broad and narrowing later rarely happens on schedule in practice; starting minimal and adding justified access is safer.
